blocks.x: All aboard the New York Transit Museum’s Holiday Train Show! One of New York City’s most magical winter traditions is chugging back into Grand Central Terminal this November 2026, with festive art, gifts for transit fans of all ages, and an enchanting display of model trains.

A beloved staple of NYC’s holiday festivities since 2002, this year’s free exhibition brings classic Lionel trains—including Metro-North, vintage subway sets, and the whimsical Polar Express—making their journey from a miniature Grand Central Terminal all the way to the snowy North Pole.
For locals and tourists seeking free holiday events in NYC, here’s everything you need to know before you go.
What to expect at the 2026 NYC Holiday Train Show

Lionel model trains have been a cherished part of American childhood for more than a century. Today, the New York Transit Museum’s display remains the only free train exhibition of its kind in the city, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors each year.
Visitors to the 2026 exhibition can expect:
Vintage Lionel Trains: Watch as these iconic models zip along a 34-foot, two-level “O” gauge layout, passing familiar New York landmarks on their journey to the North Pole

Economy Candy: A nod to the family-owned candy shop established in 1937, which has delighted generations of New Yorkers. It makes a fitting, nostalgic addition to this miniature city filled with familiar memories

The New York Transit Museum Store: Get a head start on holiday gift-giving with exclusive subway route t-shirts, Munipals wooden train toys, authentic token jewelry, cozy subway map blankets, and more transit-themed gifts

Source / Filip Wolak, via New York Transit Museum
New for 2026: Danny Cortes’ miniature NYC landmarks

This year’s display elevates the artistry with a brand new section of buildings crafted by NYC-based artist Danny Cortes. A revered creator of miniature models, Cortes draws inspiration from the gritty, everyday details that make New York special—from weathered storefronts and historic architecture to the fleeting moments New Yorkers often take for granted.

His masterpieces feature weathered brickwork, intricate storefront signage, and carefully recreated architectural features that capture the character of New York’s diverse neighborhoods. Highlights include:
Crazy Eddie: The iconic electronics chain that once operated 43 stores across the Northeast
La Borinqueña: A beloved family-owned grocery store in South Williamsburg that closed in 2013, complete with Puerto Rican flags beneath its awning
Classic NYC Architecture: Two apartment buildings featuring ornate cornices and rows of highly detailed windows
Eric’s Comic Books: A charming, fictional neighborhood staple
Cortes stated:
During the holidays, it feels like the city comes alive in a completely different way. I hope when people see these models, they feel a little bit of that magic.

MTA New York City Transit / Marc A. Hermann
Event details: Dates, times, & location
What: New York Transit Museum Holiday Train Show
Where: New York Transit Museum Grand Central Gallery & Store (located in the shuttle passage on 42nd Street and Park Avenue)
When: On view Friday, November 13, 2026 – February 2027
Hours: Monday – Friday, 10 am to 7:30 pm | Saturday & Sunday, 10 am to 6 pm
Admission: 100% Free
Don’t miss the chance to see miniature NYC, the Polar Express, and the snow-covered North Pole all in one enchanting display!
